Three college kids just wanted to knock rival Minecraft servers offline. Instead, they blacked out Twitter, Netflix, and PayPal across the entire East Coast.

This is the story of Mirai — the botnet that didn't need supercomputers. It hunted the internet's weakest, most forgotten devices: webcams, DVRs, and baby monitors still running factory default passwords. Paras Jha and his friends infected hundreds of thousands of them, then aimed the entire swarm at Dyn, the DNS provider that acts like the phone book of the web. When Dyn went down, half the internet went dark with it.

The lesson every developer should remember: the biggest DDoS attack in history wasn't built from power — it was built from the devices you forgot were plugged in.
